+            ${{ runner.temp }}/context.json
+            ${{ runner.temp }}/*-tests.json

+# v0.2.0 archival supplement and offline reproduction
+
+The accepted release is `d8a4ffb5b63eb9359a4c0af9134b4f9a3c529618`, tree
+`72ad841cc5b3cffc5f82979a9739b7fd03d75e15`. Its existing 29 release files
+and original ZIP remain unchanged. A supplement stores history and later
+captures separately; it introduces no theorem or scientific acceptance.
+
+## Constructing supplement-1
+
+Acquire the original R C10 ZIP and final captures before packaging. Acquisition
+is the only online evidence step. The fixed original ZIP has 9,377 bytes and
+SHA-256 `75d61c01020f63d7f9555f10f32de9d63a09c0107536463ae549cdb85ebe9fc8`.
+Its artifact ID is `12106535829`, run `39045919534`. A new workflow run cannot
+replace those historical bytes. Never put credentials or signed redirect URLs
+in the supplement.
+
+Retain every page behind assembled review submissions and threads. Connector
+thread responses expose no pagination state, so their full saved response and
+exact PR request are cross-checked against exhaustive REST inline-comment pages
+and the captured PR comment count. Do not invent a completion flag. Each final
+job needs its own nonempty, source-bound log capture; an unopened run-level ZIP
+cannot substitute for those logs.
+
+Commit clean tooling at T first. Then, from the repository root:
+
+```text
+python -B -m verification.archive.create_bundle --repo . --evidence CAPTURE_DIR --output NEW_EXTERNAL_DIRECTORY
+```
+
+The builder derives 36 named refs / 26 distinct input commits from the accepted
+seven source receipts and the fixed final R identities. The separate registry
+ZIP mentioned in the supplied audit was not attached locally: the delivered
+registry explicitly labels this derivation, without claiming byte identity to
+the unavailable registry. Its namespace is `refs/archive/permansson/v0.2.0/`.
+
+Only those exact refs enter a disposable staging repository. The full bundle
+contains their reachable history, including all eight synthetic merges, without
+prerequisites. The full object inventory records canonical payload hashes; it
+does not confuse 26 input commit identities with the much larger closure.
+
+The historical bundle excludes T and all subsequent maintenance commits.
+Tooling from T is a content-hashed file snapshot alongside the bundle. After
+verification, commit supplement files separately. Later tooling changes require
+updating that snapshot; stale copies are rejected. Record eventual maintenance
+H/B/S/M, review, rollout and publication in an external acceptance receipt.
+
+The snapshot includes this canonical guide. Candidate-bound replay compares the
+complete code and guide closure at T and current checkout C, then checks the
+executing code and delivered copies. `OFFLINE_REPRODUCTION.md` must exactly
+match the guide snapshot. These comparisons use committed Git content for the
+guide, so checkout newline conversion does not alter its source identity.
+
+Candidate-bound replay also checks the committed publication-candidate ZIP and
+checksum against the complete committed supplement at C. Every delivered inner
+file must match that same canonical snapshot, including the manifest and its
+checksum. The ZIP must contain exactly those bytes with the documented sorted
+inventory, regular modes and fixed timestamps. Repaired sidecar hashes cannot
+make a stale or altered ZIP acceptable. Standalone artifact replay has no
+candidate repository and explicitly does not perform this publication check.
+
+## Supported offline profile
+
+Install Python 3.13, Git and `pypdf==6.10.0` before the isolation boundary.
+ReportLab, matplotlib, Lean and mathlib are not prerequisites for artifact replay.
+Run as a nonroot Linux user with the reviewed `/usr/bin/sudo`, `unshare` and
+`setpriv` adapter available:
+
+```text
+python -B -m verification.archive.offline_smoke --repo . --candidate FULL_SHA --supplement SUPPLEMENT_DIRECTORY --scratch NEW_EMPTY_DIRECTORY --report REPORT_OUTSIDE_SOURCE.json
+```
+
+The adapter creates a fresh network namespace and drops to the original UID/GID
+with no supplementary groups or capabilities and no-new-privileges before
+parsing candidate inputs. It records different parent/child namespaces, no
+external route and a conclusively denied outward socket. Unavailable isolation
+returns BLOCKED/nonzero. There is no online fallback. Windows may run portable
+Git fixture tests, but cannot claim this Linux isolation acceptance.
+
+For a standalone supplement, change into its `tooling/` directory and run:
+
+```text
+python -B -m verification.archive.offline_smoke --supplement .. --scratch ABSOLUTE_NEW_EMPTY_DIRECTORY --report ABSOLUTE_REPORT.json
+```
+
+This requires no prior Git checkout. After successful restoration its local
+context is captured from the actual restored A and explicitly labeled
+`accepted_artifact_replay`. Candidate-context CI acceptance still requires the
+real maintenance Git checkout and genuine event. A standalone replay report
+cannot replace current candidate CI.
+
+Standalone replay compares the delivered code and guide copies by content; it
+does not discover a surrounding Git repository or authenticate the publisher.
+Both `--repo` and `--candidate` are required together for candidate-bound use.
+
+## What the archival gate proves
+
+The gate validates all delivered hashes and inventories; rejects unsafe paths,
+symlinks, extra files and unbounded input; checks a prerequisite-free v2 header;
+imports into an empty object database; runs full strict Git object checking;
+and compares exact refs, full objects, ordered merge parents, matching synthetic
+and main trees, ancestry and accepted tree.
+
+Fixed file-count, directory-count, depth and aggregate-byte budgets apply during
+the filesystem metadata walk, before hashing payloads. Per-file streaming limits
+also reject files that grow after metadata preflight.
+
+It restores accepted A using canonical normal blobs, rechecks all 369 pins and
+the complete deterministic TeX export, then runs the unchanged final release
+verifier, package checker with `--verify`, all 29 old release tests and original
+R C10 arithmetic/generated-source/transcript consistency validation. It rehashes
+accepted artifacts and all delivered files afterward.
+
+Distinguish the following results:
+
+- Source restoration: historical objects, refs, parent relations and trees.
+- Artifact replay: existing kit and captured evidence rechecked at A.
+- Fresh Lean execution: not performed by this replay; requires the pinned proof
+  environment and separate current candidate workflow evidence.
+- Publisher authentication: not created by an offline checksum, copied JSON,
+  or code-review comment. The R digest is compared with the separately fixed
+  publisher identity. The archived final review remains a code-review artifact.
+
+`git bundle verify` alone is insufficient: an intact header can outlive a
+truncated pack. Successful import, object checking and source binding are also
+mandatory. Different Git versions need not regenerate identical pack bytes;
+the delivered bundle digest is fixed, while independent reconstruction must
+match its exact object/ref closure.
+
+## Completion boundaries
+
+Prepared code, actual offline restoration, active repository enforcement,
+verified remote tag and retrieved external publication are distinct stages.
+Proposed disabled rules, local supplements and expiring Actions uploads do not
+close operational F3. No setting, remote ref or publication is changed by these
+tools. Those operations require their separately authorized rollout.

+# v0.2.0 archival supplement and offline reproduction
+
+The accepted release is `d8a4ffb5b63eb9359a4c0af9134b4f9a3c529618`, tree
+`72ad841cc5b3cffc5f82979a9739b7fd03d75e15`. Its existing 29 release files
+and original ZIP remain unchanged. A supplement stores history and later
+captures separately; it introduces no theorem or scientific acceptance.
+
+## Constructing supplement-1
+
+Acquire the original R C10 ZIP and final captures before packaging. Acquisition
+is the only online evidence step. The fixed original ZIP has 9,377 bytes and
+SHA-256 `75d61c01020f63d7f9555f10f32de9d63a09c0107536463ae549cdb85ebe9fc8`.
+Its artifact ID is `12106535829`, run `39045919534`. A new workflow run cannot
+replace those historical bytes. Never put credentials or signed redirect URLs
+in the supplement.
+
+Retain every page behind assembled review submissions and threads. Connector
+thread responses expose no pagination state, so their full saved response and
+exact PR request are cross-checked against exhaustive REST inline-comment pages
+and the captured PR comment count. Do not invent a completion flag. Each final
+job needs its own nonempty, source-bound log capture; an unopened run-level ZIP
+cannot substitute for those logs.
+
+Commit clean tooling at T first. Then, from the repository root:
+
+```text
+python -B -m verification.archive.create_bundle --repo . --evidence CAPTURE_DIR --output NEW_EXTERNAL_DIRECTORY
+```
+
+The builder derives 36 named refs / 26 distinct input commits from the accepted
+seven source receipts and the fixed final R identities. The separate registry
+ZIP mentioned in the supplied audit was not attached locally: the delivered
+registry explicitly labels this derivation, without claiming byte identity to
+the unavailable registry. Its namespace is `refs/archive/permansson/v0.2.0/`.
+
+Only those exact refs enter a disposable staging repository. The full bundle
+contains their reachable history, including all eight synthetic merges, without
+prerequisites. The full object inventory records canonical payload hashes; it
+does not confuse 26 input commit identities with the much larger closure.
+
+The historical bundle excludes T and all subsequent maintenance commits.
+Tooling from T is a content-hashed file snapshot alongside the bundle. After
+verification, commit supplement files separately. Later tooling changes require
+updating that snapshot; stale copies are rejected. Record eventual maintenance
+H/B/S/M, review, rollout and publication in an external acceptance receipt.
+
+The snapshot includes this canonical guide. Candidate-bound replay compares the
+complete code and guide closure at T and current checkout C, then checks the
+executing code and delivered copies. `OFFLINE_REPRODUCTION.md` must exactly
+match the guide snapshot. These comparisons use committed Git content for the
+guide, so checkout newline conversion does not alter its source identity.
+
+Candidate-bound replay also checks the committed publication-candidate ZIP and
+checksum against the complete committed supplement at C. Every delivered inner
+file must match that same canonical snapshot, including the manifest and its
+checksum. The ZIP must contain exactly those bytes with the documented sorted
+inventory, regular modes and fixed timestamps. Repaired sidecar hashes cannot
+make a stale or altered ZIP acceptable. Standalone artifact replay has no
+candidate repository and explicitly does not perform this publication check.
+
+## Supported offline profile
+
+Install Python 3.13, Git and `pypdf==6.10.0` before the isolation boundary.
+ReportLab, matplotlib, Lean and mathlib are not prerequisites for artifact replay.
+Run as a nonroot Linux user with the reviewed `/usr/bin/sudo`, `unshare` and
+`setpriv` adapter available:
+
+```text
+python -B -m verification.archive.offline_smoke --repo . --candidate FULL_SHA --supplement SUPPLEMENT_DIRECTORY --scratch NEW_EMPTY_DIRECTORY --report REPORT_OUTSIDE_SOURCE.json
+```
+
+The adapter creates a fresh network namespace and drops to the original UID/GID
+with no supplementary groups or capabilities and no-new-privileges before
+parsing candidate inputs. It records different parent/child namespaces, no
+external route and a conclusively denied outward socket. Unavailable isolation
+returns BLOCKED/nonzero. There is no online fallback. Windows may run portable
+Git fixture tests, but cannot claim this Linux isolation acceptance.
+
+For a standalone supplement, change into its `tooling/` directory and run:
+
+```text
+python -B -m verification.archive.offline_smoke --supplement .. --scratch ABSOLUTE_NEW_EMPTY_DIRECTORY --report ABSOLUTE_REPORT.json
+```
+
+This requires no prior Git checkout. After successful restoration its local
+context is captured from the actual restored A and explicitly labeled
+`accepted_artifact_replay`. Candidate-context CI acceptance still requires the
+real maintenance Git checkout and genuine event. A standalone replay report
+cannot replace current candidate CI.
+
+Standalone replay compares the delivered code and guide copies by content; it
+does not discover a surrounding Git repository or authenticate the publisher.
+Both `--repo` and `--candidate` are required together for candidate-bound use.
+
+## What the archival gate proves
+
+The gate validates all delivered hashes and inventories; rejects unsafe paths,
+symlinks, extra files and unbounded input; checks a prerequisite-free v2 header;
+imports into an empty object database; runs full strict Git object checking;
+and compares exact refs, full objects, ordered merge parents, matching synthetic
+and main trees, ancestry and accepted tree.
+
+Fixed file-count, directory-count, depth and aggregate-byte budgets apply during
+the filesystem metadata walk, before hashing payloads. Per-file streaming limits
+also reject files that grow after metadata preflight.
+
+It restores accepted A using canonical normal blobs, rechecks all 369 pins and
+the complete deterministic TeX export, then runs the unchanged final release
+verifier, package checker with `--verify`, all 29 old release tests and original
+R C10 arithmetic/generated-source/transcript consistency validation. It rehashes
+accepted artifacts and all delivered files afterward.
+
+Distinguish the following results:
+
+- Source restoration: historical objects, refs, parent relations and trees.
+- Artifact replay: existing kit and captured evidence rechecked at A.
+- Fresh Lean execution: not performed by this replay; requires the pinned proof
+  environment and separate current candidate workflow evidence.
+- Publisher authentication: not created by an offline checksum, copied JSON,
+  or code-review comment. The R digest is compared with the separately fixed
+  publisher identity. The archived final review remains a code-review artifact.
+
+`git bundle verify` alone is insufficient: an intact header can outlive a
+truncated pack. Successful import, object checking and source binding are also
+mandatory. Different Git versions need not regenerate identical pack bytes;
+the delivered bundle digest is fixed, while independent reconstruction must
+match its exact object/ref closure.
+
+## Completion boundaries
+
+Prepared code, actual offline restoration, active repository enforcement,
+verified remote tag and retrieved external publication are distinct stages.
+Proposed disabled rules, local supplements and expiring Actions uploads do not
+close operational F3. No setting, remote ref or publication is changed by these
+tools. Those operations require their separately authorized rollout.

+# v0.2.0 archival supplement and offline reproduction
+
+The accepted release is `d8a4ffb5b63eb9359a4c0af9134b4f9a3c529618`, tree
+`72ad841cc5b3cffc5f82979a9739b7fd03d75e15`. Its existing 29 release files
+and original ZIP remain unchanged. A supplement stores history and later
+captures separately; it introduces no theorem or scientific acceptance.
+
+## Constructing supplement-1
+
+Acquire the original R C10 ZIP and final captures before packaging. Acquisition
+is the only online evidence step. The fixed original ZIP has 9,377 bytes and
+SHA-256 `75d61c01020f63d7f9555f10f32de9d63a09c0107536463ae549cdb85ebe9fc8`.
+Its artifact ID is `12106535829`, run `39045919534`. A new workflow run cannot
+replace those historical bytes. Never put credentials or signed redirect URLs
+in the supplement.
+
+Retain every page behind assembled review submissions and threads. Connector
+thread responses expose no pagination state, so their full saved response and
+exact PR request are cross-checked against exhaustive REST inline-comment pages
+and the captured PR comment count. Do not invent a completion flag. Each final
+job needs its own nonempty, source-bound log capture; an unopened run-level ZIP
+cannot substitute for those logs.
+
+Commit clean tooling at T first. Then, from the repository root:
+
+```text
+python -B -m verification.archive.create_bundle --repo . --evidence CAPTURE_DIR --output NEW_EXTERNAL_DIRECTORY
+```
+
+The builder derives 36 named refs / 26 distinct input commits from the accepted
+seven source receipts and the fixed final R identities. The separate registry
+ZIP mentioned in the supplied audit was not attached locally: the delivered
+registry explicitly labels this derivation, without claiming byte identity to
+the unavailable registry. Its namespace is `refs/archive/permansson/v0.2.0/`.
+
+Only those exact refs enter a disposable staging repository. The full bundle
+contains their reachable history, including all eight synthetic merges, without
+prerequisites. The full object inventory records canonical payload hashes; it
+does not confuse 26 input commit identities with the much larger closure.
+
+The historical bundle excludes T and all subsequent maintenance commits.
+Tooling from T is a content-hashed file snapshot alongside the bundle. After
+verification, commit supplement files separately. Later tooling changes require
+updating that snapshot; stale copies are rejected. Record eventual maintenance
+H/B/S/M, review, rollout and publication in an external acceptance receipt.
+
+The snapshot includes this canonical guide. Candidate-bound replay compares the
+complete code and guide closure at T and current checkout C, then checks the
+executing code and delivered copies. `OFFLINE_REPRODUCTION.md` must exactly
+match the guide snapshot. These comparisons use committed Git content for the
+guide, so checkout newline conversion does not alter its source identity.
+
+Candidate-bound replay also checks the committed publication-candidate ZIP and
+checksum against the complete committed supplement at C. Every delivered inner
+file must match that same canonical snapshot, including the manifest and its
+checksum. The ZIP must contain exactly those bytes with the documented sorted
+inventory, regular modes and fixed timestamps. Repaired sidecar hashes cannot
+make a stale or altered ZIP acceptable. Standalone artifact replay has no
+candidate repository and explicitly does not perform this publication check.
+
+## Supported offline profile
+
+Install Python 3.13, Git and `pypdf==6.10.0` before the isolation boundary.
+ReportLab, matplotlib, Lean and mathlib are not prerequisites for artifact replay.
+Run as a nonroot Linux user with the reviewed `/usr/bin/sudo`, `unshare` and
+`setpriv` adapter available:
+
+```text
+python -B -m verification.archive.offline_smoke --repo . --candidate FULL_SHA --supplement SUPPLEMENT_DIRECTORY --scratch NEW_EMPTY_DIRECTORY --report REPORT_OUTSIDE_SOURCE.json
+```
+
+The adapter creates a fresh network namespace and drops to the original UID/GID
+with no supplementary groups or capabilities and no-new-privileges before
+parsing candidate inputs. It records different parent/child namespaces, no
+external route and a conclusively denied outward socket. Unavailable isolation
+returns BLOCKED/nonzero. There is no online fallback. Windows may run portable
+Git fixture tests, but cannot claim this Linux isolation acceptance.
+
+For a standalone supplement, change into its `tooling/` directory and run:
+
+```text
+python -B -m verification.archive.offline_smoke --supplement .. --scratch ABSOLUTE_NEW_EMPTY_DIRECTORY --report ABSOLUTE_REPORT.json
+```
+
+This requires no prior Git checkout. After successful restoration its local
+context is captured from the actual restored A and explicitly labeled
+`accepted_artifact_replay`. Candidate-context CI acceptance still requires the
+real maintenance Git checkout and genuine event. A standalone replay report
+cannot replace current candidate CI.
+
+Standalone replay compares the delivered code and guide copies by content; it
+does not discover a surrounding Git repository or authenticate the publisher.
+Both `--repo` and `--candidate` are required together for candidate-bound use.
+
+## What the archival gate proves
+
+The gate validates all delivered hashes and inventories; rejects unsafe paths,
+symlinks, extra files and unbounded input; checks a prerequisite-free v2 header;
+imports into an empty object database; runs full strict Git object checking;
+and compares exact refs, full objects, ordered merge parents, matching synthetic
+and main trees, ancestry and accepted tree.
+
+Fixed file-count, directory-count, depth and aggregate-byte budgets apply during
+the filesystem metadata walk, before hashing payloads. Per-file streaming limits
+also reject files that grow after metadata preflight.
+
+It restores accepted A using canonical normal blobs, rechecks all 369 pins and
+the complete deterministic TeX export, then runs the unchanged final release
+verifier, package checker with `--verify`, all 29 old release tests and original
+R C10 arithmetic/generated-source/transcript consistency validation. It rehashes
+accepted artifacts and all delivered files afterward.
+
+Distinguish the following results:
+
+- Source restoration: historical objects, refs, parent relations and trees.
+- Artifact replay: existing kit and captured evidence rechecked at A.
+- Fresh Lean execution: not performed by this replay; requires the pinned proof
+  environment and separate current candidate workflow evidence.
+- Publisher authentication: not created by an offline checksum, copied JSON,
+  or code-review comment. The R digest is compared with the separately fixed
+  publisher identity. The archived final review remains a code-review artifact.
+
+`git bundle verify` alone is insufficient: an intact header can outlive a
+truncated pack. Successful import, object checking and source binding are also
+mandatory. Different Git versions need not regenerate identical pack bytes;
+the delivered bundle digest is fixed, while independent reconstruction must
+match its exact object/ref closure.
+
+## Completion boundaries
+
+Prepared code, actual offline restoration, active repository enforcement,
+verified remote tag and retrieved external publication are distinct stages.
+Proposed disabled rules, local supplements and expiring Actions uploads do not
+close operational F3. No setting, remote ref or publication is changed by these
+tools. Those operations require their separately authorized rollout.

+"""Privilege-dropped worker; attest isolation before parsing a supplement."""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+import sys
+
+# A direct script invocation needs only this known source root, never cwd or
+# candidate PYTHONPATH. The launcher has already dropped all root privileges.
+sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))
+
+from verification.integrity.reports import HardeningError, check_report, write_report
+from verification.archive.offline_smoke import isolation_attestation
+from verification.archive.verify_bundle import verify_supplement
+
+
+def main(argv=None):
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--supplement", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--scratch", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--report", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--parent-netns", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--source-repo")
+    parser.add_argument("--source-candidate")
+    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
+    try:
+        isolation = isolation_attestation(args.parent_netns)
+        os.environ["PERMANSSON_PARENT_NETNS"] = args.parent_netns
+        details = verify_supplement(args.supplement, args.scratch, require_isolation=True,
+                                    source_repo=args.source_repo, source_candidate=args.source_candidate)
+        details["isolation"] = isolation
+        payload = check_report("archive-reproducibility", details=details,
+                               completed_stages=details["completed_stages"])
+        code = 0
+    except HardeningError as exc:
+        payload = check_report("archive-reproducibility", None, "BLOCKED" if exc.exit_code == 3 else "FAIL", exc)
+        code = exc.exit_code
+    except Exception as exc:
+        payload = check_report("archive-reproducibility", None, "FAIL", HardeningError("E_UNEXPECTED", str(exc)))
+        code = 1
+    write_report(args.report, payload)
+    return code
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

+"""Bounded, strict supplement inventories. Checksums do not authenticate publishers."""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import hashlib
+import json
+import os
+from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath
+import re
+import stat
+
+from verification.integrity.reports import HardeningError
+
+FORMAT = "Permansson.Hardening.Archive.v1"
+MAX_METADATA = 8 * 1024 * 1024
+MAX_BUNDLE = 256 * 1024 * 1024
+MAX_OBJECT = 128 * 1024 * 1024
+MAX_CLOSURE = 1024 * 1024 * 1024
+MAX_OBJECTS = 200_000
+# Fixed delivered-filesystem budgets, independent of Git object closure.
+# The normal supplement is far below these ceilings.
+MAX_FILES = 2048
+MAX_TOTAL_BYTES = 512 * 1024 * 1024
+MAX_DIRECTORIES = 2048
+MAX_DIRECTORY_DEPTH = 128
+SHA = re.compile(r"[0-9a-f]{40}\Z")
+SHA256 = re.compile(r"[0-9a-f]{64}\Z")
+SELF_FILES = {"archive-manifest.json", "archive-manifest.sha256"}
+
+
+def fail(code, message, exit_code=1):
+    raise HardeningError(code, message, exit_code)
+
+
+def stable_json(value):
+    return (json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=True, sort_keys=True, indent=2) + "\n").encode()
+
+
+def digest(data):
+    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
+
+
+def atomic_json(path, value):
+    path = Path(path)
+    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    temporary = path.with_name(path.name + f".{os.getpid()}.tmp")
+    try:
+        with temporary.open("xb") as stream:
+            stream.write(stable_json(value))
+        os.replace(temporary, path)
+    finally:
+        temporary.unlink(missing_ok=True)
+

+def strict_json(data, code="E_MANIFEST_FORMAT"):
+    if len(data) > MAX_METADATA:
+        fail("E_LIMIT", "JSON metadata exceeds the fixed 8 MiB budget")
+    def pairs(rows):
+        result = {}
+        for key, value in rows:
+            if key in result:
+                fail(code, "Duplicate JSON key: " + key)
+            result[key] = value
+        return result
+    try:
+        return json.loads(data.decode("utf-8"), object_pairs_hook=pairs,
+                          parse_constant=lambda value: fail(code, "Non-finite JSON number"))
+    except (ValueError, UnicodeError) as exc:
+        fail(code, "Invalid UTF-8 JSON: " + str(exc))
+
+
+def safe_path(value):
+    if (not isinstance(value, str) or not value or "\\" in value or ":" in value
+            or any(ord(c) < 32 for c in value) or value.startswith("/")):
+        fail("E_MANIFEST_FORMAT", "Unsafe delivered path")
+    parts = value.split("/")
+    if any(part in {"", ".", ".."} for part in parts) or str(PurePosixPath(value)) != value:
+        fail("E_MANIFEST_FORMAT", "Noncanonical delivered path: " + value)
+    return value

+    path = Path(path)
+    if path.is_symlink() or not path.is_file():
+        fail("E_MANIFEST_FORMAT", "Expected a regular delivered file: " + str(path))
+    if path.stat().st_size > limit:
+        fail("E_LIMIT", "Delivered file exceeds its size budget: " + str(path))
+    with path.open("rb") as stream:
+        data = stream.read(limit + 1)
+    if len(data) > limit:
+        fail("E_LIMIT", "Delivered file grew beyond its size budget")
+    return data
+
+

+        if size != expected_size:

+            if observed_size > limit:
+                fail("E_LIMIT", "Delivered payload grew beyond its size budget: " + relative)
+            hasher.update(chunk)

+        fail("E_MANIFEST_FORMAT", "Delivered payload changed during inventory: " + relative)

+"""Bind the committed publication candidate to the verified canonical supplement."""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from io import BytesIO
+from pathlib import Path
+import stat
+import struct
+import zipfile
+import zlib
+
+from verification.integrity.reports import HardeningError
+from .create_bundle import ACCEPTED, ACCEPTED_TREE
+from .manifest import MAX_BUNDLE, MAX_CLOSURE, MAX_METADATA, SELF_FILES, digest, fail, read_bounded, safe_path
+
+SUPPLEMENT_PREFIX = "archival/v0.2.0/supplement-1/"
+ZIP_PATH = "archival/v0.2.0/publication-candidate/Permansson_v0.2.0_archival-supplement-1.zip"
+MAX_PUBLICATION_FILES = 4096
+FIXED_TIME = (2026, 10, 17, 0, 0, 0)
+
+
+def _reject(message):
+    fail("E_PUBLICATION_INTEGRITY", message)
+
+
+def _verify_zip(payload, expected):
+    """Bound classic-ZIP parsing before opening its central directory; never extract."""
+    if len(payload) > MAX_BUNDLE or len(payload) < 22 or payload[-22:-18] != b"PK\x05\x06":
+        _reject("Publication ZIP exceeds budget or lacks an empty-comment classic ZIP end record")
+    _, disk, directory_disk, disk_count, count, size, offset, comment = struct.unpack("<4s4H2LH", payload[-22:])
+    if (disk or directory_disk or comment or count != disk_count or count == 65535
+            or count != len(expected) or count > MAX_PUBLICATION_FILES
+            or offset + size != len(payload) - 22 or not payload.startswith(b"PK\x03\x04")):
+        _reject("Publication ZIP has an unsupported, unbounded or inconsistent directory")
+    # Do not trust the EOCD count before ZipFile allocates its ZipInfo objects.
+    # A repaired end record could conceal many more actual directory entries.
+    cursor, observed, end = offset, 0, offset + size
+    while cursor < end:
+        if cursor + 46 > end or payload[cursor:cursor + 4] != b"PK\x01\x02":
+            _reject("Malformed publication central-directory record")
+        name_size, extra_size, comment_size = struct.unpack_from("<3H", payload, cursor + 28)
+        observed += 1
+        cursor += 46 + name_size + extra_size + comment_size
+        if observed > count or observed > MAX_PUBLICATION_FILES or cursor > end:
+            _reject("Publication central-directory inventory exceeds its declared fixed budget")
+    if cursor != end or observed != count:
+        _reject("Publication central-directory count differs from the end record")
+    try:
+        with zipfile.ZipFile(BytesIO(payload)) as archive:
+            entries = archive.infolist()
+            if [entry.filename for entry in entries] != sorted(expected) or archive.comment:
+                _reject("Publication ZIP member inventory/order differs from canonical C")
+            local_cursor = 0
+            for entry in entries:
+                name = entry.filename
+                try:
+                    safe_path(name)
+                except HardeningError as exc:
+                    raise HardeningError("E_PUBLICATION_INTEGRITY", "Unsafe publication ZIP member path") from exc
+                content = expected[name]
+                if (entry.orig_filename != name or entry.is_dir() or entry.flag_bits & ~0x800 or entry.create_system != 3
+                        or entry.external_attr >> 16 != stat.S_IFREG | 0o644
+                        or entry.date_time != FIXED_TIME or entry.extra or entry.comment
+                        or entry.compress_type not in {zipfile.ZIP_STORED, zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED}
+                        or entry.file_size != len(content) or entry.header_offset >= offset):
+                    _reject("Publication ZIP member has unsafe metadata or an unexpected size: " + name)
+                if entry.header_offset != local_cursor or local_cursor + 30 > offset:
+                    _reject("Publication local records contain a gap, overlap or invalid offset")
+                local = struct.unpack_from("<4s5H3L2H", payload, local_cursor)
+                filename = name.encode("utf-8" if entry.flag_bits & 0x800 else "cp437")
+                if (local[:5] != (b"PK\x03\x04", entry.extract_version, entry.flag_bits, entry.compress_type, 0)
+                        or local[5] != ((2026 - 1980) << 9 | 10 << 5 | 17)
+                        or local[6:9] != (entry.CRC, entry.compress_size, entry.file_size)
+                        or local[9:] != (len(filename), 0)
+                        or payload[local_cursor + 30:local_cursor + 30 + len(filename)] != filename):
+                    _reject("Publication local metadata differs from its canonical central record")
+                local_cursor += 30 + len(filename) + entry.compress_size
+                if local_cursor > offset:
+                    _reject("Publication compressed member overlaps the central directory")
+                with archive.open(entry) as stream:
+                    actual = stream.read(len(content) + 1)
+                if actual != content:
+                    _reject("Publication ZIP member differs from canonical supplement: " + name)
+            if local_cursor != offset:
+                _reject("Publication ZIP has unreferenced bytes before its central directory")
+    except (zipfile.BadZipFile, zlib.error, RuntimeError, NotImplementedError, OSError, ValueError, EOFError) as exc:
+        raise HardeningError("E_PUBLICATION_INTEGRITY", "Cannot safely read publication ZIP") from exc
+
+
+def validate_committed_publication(repo, candidate, supplement, manifest):
+    """Authority is canonical C, including both manifest files and every inner path."""
+    repo.validate_candidate(candidate, accepted_sha=ACCEPTED, accepted_tree=ACCEPTED_TREE)
+    if repo.run("rev-parse", "HEAD").decode().strip() != candidate:
+        _reject("Publication candidate differs from current checkout HEAD")
+    tree = repo.tree(candidate)
+    prefix = SUPPLEMENT_PREFIX.encode()
+    entries = {path[len(prefix):].decode("utf-8"): entry for path, entry in tree.items() if path.startswith(prefix)}
+    expected_names = {row["path"] for row in manifest["files"]} | SELF_FILES
+    if not entries or len(entries) > MAX_PUBLICATION_FILES or set(entries) != expected_names:
+        _reject("Committed supplement path set differs from the verified delivered inventory")
+    expected, total = {}, 0
+    for name, entry in entries.items():
+        safe_path(name)
+        if entry.object_type != "blob" or entry.mode != "100644":
+            _reject("Committed supplement contains a nonregular or non-0644 path")
+        limit = MAX_BUNDLE if name == "history.bundle" else MAX_METADATA
+        content = repo.blob(entry.oid, limit=limit)
+        total += len(content)
+        if total > MAX_CLOSURE:
+            _reject("Canonical supplement exceeds its aggregate byte budget")
+        if read_bounded(Path(supplement) / name, limit) != content:
+            _reject("Verified supplement filesystem differs from committed C: " + name)
+        expected[name] = content
+    archive, sidecar = tree.get(ZIP_PATH.encode()), tree.get((ZIP_PATH + ".sha256").encode())
+    if any(entry is None or entry.object_type != "blob" or entry.mode != "100644" for entry in (archive, sidecar)):
+        _reject("Committed publication ZIP and checksum must be regular 0644 blobs")
+    payload = repo.blob(archive.oid, limit=MAX_BUNDLE)
+    checksum = repo.blob(sidecar.oid, limit=256)
+    if checksum != (digest(payload) + "  " + Path(ZIP_PATH).name + "\n").encode("ascii"):
+        _reject("Committed publication ZIP checksum differs")
+    _verify_zip(payload, expected)
+    return {"status": "PASS", "scope": "canonical_candidate_objects", "candidate": candidate,
+            "zip_path": ZIP_PATH, "zip_blob": archive.oid, "sidecar_blob": sidecar.oid,

+class Graph:
+    def __init__(self, root):
+        self.root = Path(root)
+        subprocess.run([shutil.which("git"), "-c", "init.templateDir=", "init", "--bare", str(self.root)],
+                       check=True, capture_output=True, timeout=60)
+        self.repo = GitRepo(self.root)
+        self.repo.run("config", "user.name", "Archive fixture")
+        self.repo.run("config", "user.email", "archive@example.invalid")
+        self.t0 = self.tree(b"base\n")
+        self.base = self.commit(self.t0, [], "base")
+        self.t1 = self.tree(b"head\n")
+        self.head = self.commit(self.t1, [self.base], "head")
+        self.synthetic = self.commit(self.t1, [self.base, self.head], "synthetic")
+        self.main = self.commit(self.t1, [self.base, self.head], "main")
+        self.registry = {"refs": [{"ref": REF_PREFIX + name, "commit": oid}
+                                  for name, oid in sorted({"base": self.base, "head": self.head,
+                                                          "synthetic": self.synthetic, "main": self.main}.items())],
+                         "milestones": [{"anchor": "fixture", "head": self.head, "base": self.base,
+                                         "synthetic": self.synthetic, "main": self.main}]}
+
+    def tree(self, payload):
+        blob = self.repo.run("hash-object", "-w", "--stdin", input=payload).strip().decode()
+        return self.repo.run("mktree", input=("100644 blob " + blob + "\tfile.txt\n").encode()).strip().decode()
+
+    def commit(self, tree, parents, message):
+        args = ["commit-tree", tree]
+        for parent in parents:
+            args.extend(["-p", parent])
+        return self.repo.run(*args, input=(message + "\n").encode()).strip().decode()

+        while True:

+                fail("E_BUNDLE_REFS", "Malformed or unbounded bundle header")
+            if line == b"\n":

+            if line.startswith(b"-"):

+            if line.startswith(b"@"):

+"""Fresh isolated harness for the accepted TeX function; never builds artifacts."""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import hashlib
+import importlib
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+import sys
+
+
+def _fail(code, message):
+    sys.stderr.write("PERMANSSON_TEX_ERROR " + json.dumps({"code": code, "message": message}) + "\n")
+    return 1
+
+
+def main(argv=None):
+    args = sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv
+    if len(args) != 6:
+        return _fail("E_EXPORT_REFERENCE", "Invalid internal worker invocation")
+    directory, revision, manuscript_hash, builder_hash, verifier_hash, manuscript_name = args
+    trusted = Path(directory).resolve(strict=True)
+    try:
+        if not sys.flags.isolated or not sys.flags.no_site or not sys.flags.dont_write_bytecode:
+            return _fail("E_IMPORT_ORIGIN", "Worker requires -I -S -B")
+        for name, expected in (("build_release.py", builder_hash), ("verify_release.py", verifier_hash),
+                               (manuscript_name, manuscript_hash)):
+            path = trusted / name
+            if path.parent != trusted or path.is_symlink() or not path.is_file():
+                return _fail("E_REFERENCE_MISSING", "Trusted input is absent or not a regular file")
+            if hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest() != expected:
+                return _fail("E_EXPORT_REFERENCE", "Trusted input digest mismatch")
+        # -I -S excludes cwd, PYTHONPATH, user site and startup hooks. The only
+        # added import location is the fresh directory populated by the parent.
+        sys.path.insert(0, str(trusted))
+        if "build_release" in sys.modules or "verify_release" in sys.modules:
+            return _fail("E_IMPORT_ORIGIN", "Reference modules were already imported")
+        builder = importlib.import_module("build_release")
+        verifier = importlib.import_module("verify_release")
+        for module, name in ((builder, "build_release.py"), (verifier, "verify_release.py")):
+            if Path(module.__file__).resolve(strict=True) != trusted / name:
+                return _fail("E_IMPORT_ORIGIN", "Reference module has an unexpected import origin")
+        manuscript = (trusted / manuscript_name).read_bytes()
+        if hashlib.sha256(manuscript).hexdigest() != manuscript_hash:
+            return _fail("E_EXPORT_REFERENCE", "Manuscript changed before rendering")
+        result = builder.tex_document(json.loads(manuscript), revision, manuscript_hash, False)
+        if not isinstance(result, str):
+            return _fail("E_EXPORT_REFERENCE", "Renderer did not return text")
+        sys.stdout.buffer.write(result.encode("utf-8"))
+        sys.stdout.buffer.flush()
+        return 0
+    except Exception as exc:
+        return _fail("E_EXPORT_REFERENCE", f"Reference rendering failed: {type(exc).__name__}: {str(exc)[:1000]}")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

+"""Bind reports to canonical local objects or the actual GitHub event checkout."""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
+import hashlib
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from .git_objects import GitRepo, full_oid
+from .reports import HardeningError, strict_json, write_report
+
+REPOSITORY = "HMarcusWH/PermanssonLean"
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class CheckContext:
+    repository: str
+    accepted_release: str
+    checked_sha: str
+    checked_tree: str
+    event: str
+    pr_number: int | None = None
+    head_sha: str | None = None
+    base_sha: str | None = None
+    run_id: int | None = None
+    run_attempt: int | None = None
+    event_sha256: str | None = None
+    scope: str = "canonical_commit_objects"
+
+
+def capture_context(repo, candidate, event_file=None):
+    from .policy import ACCEPTED_RELEASE
+    full_oid(candidate)
+    commit = repo.commit(candidate)
+    actual = repo.run("rev-parse", "HEAD").strip().decode("ascii")
+    if actual != candidate:
+        raise HardeningError("E_CONTEXT", "Checkout HEAD differs from tested candidate")
+    if os.environ.get("GITHUB_ACTIONS") != "true":
+        if event_file is not None:
+            raise HardeningError("E_CONTEXT", "An event file cannot manufacture a genuine CI context")
+        return CheckContext(REPOSITORY, ACCEPTED_RELEASE, candidate, commit.tree, "local")
+    try:
+        if os.environ["GITHUB_REPOSITORY"] != REPOSITORY:
+            raise HardeningError("E_CONTEXT", "Unexpected GitHub repository")
+        if full_oid(os.environ["GITHUB_SHA"]) != candidate:
+            raise HardeningError("E_CONTEXT", "Candidate differs from the event SHA")
+        event_path = Path(os.environ["GITHUB_EVENT_PATH"])
+        if event_path.stat().st_size > 8 * 1024 * 1024:
+            raise HardeningError("E_LIMIT", "Event payload exceeds budget")
+        raw = event_path.read_bytes()
+        if event_file is not None and Path(event_file).read_bytes() != raw:
+            raise HardeningError("E_CONTEXT", "Supplied event differs from the actual event file")
+        event = strict_json(raw, "E_CONTEXT")
+        name = os.environ["GITHUB_EVENT_NAME"]
+        if event.get("repository", {}).get("full_name") != REPOSITORY:
+            raise HardeningError("E_CONTEXT", "Event repository disagrees with environment")
+        run_id, attempt = int(os.environ["GITHUB_RUN_ID"]), int(os.environ["GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT"])
+        if run_id <= 0 or attempt <= 0:
+            raise ValueError("Invalid run identity")
+        values = dict(repository=REPOSITORY, accepted_release=ACCEPTED_RELEASE,
+                      checked_sha=candidate, checked_tree=commit.tree, event=name,
+                      run_id=run_id, run_attempt=attempt, event_sha256=hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest())
+        if name == "pull_request":
+            pr = event["pull_request"]
+            head, base = full_oid(pr["head"]["sha"]), full_oid(pr["base"]["sha"])
+            number = event["number"]
+            if type(number) is not int or number <= 0:
+                raise ValueError("Invalid PR number")
+            if pr["base"]["ref"] != "main" or pr["base"]["repo"]["full_name"] != REPOSITORY:
+                raise HardeningError("E_CONTEXT", "PR does not target the intended main branch")
+            if os.environ["GITHUB_REF"] != f"refs/pull/{number}/merge":
+                raise HardeningError("E_CONTEXT", "Checkout is not the genuine PR merge ref")
+            if commit.parents != (base, head):
+                raise HardeningError("E_CONTEXT", "Synthetic merge ordered parents differ from event base/head")
+            values.update(pr_number=number, head_sha=head, base_sha=base)
+        elif name == "push":
+            if event.get("ref") != "refs/heads/main" or os.environ["GITHUB_REF"] != "refs/heads/main":
+                raise HardeningError("E_CONTEXT", "Push is not for main")
+            if event.get("after") != candidate:
+                raise HardeningError("E_CONTEXT", "Push after SHA differs from candidate")
+        elif name != "workflow_dispatch":
+            raise HardeningError("E_CONTEXT", "Unsupported CI event")
+        return CheckContext(**values)
+    except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError, OSError) as exc:
+        raise HardeningError("E_CONTEXT", f"Missing or malformed source binding: {exc}") from exc
+
+
+def require_pr_acceptance(context, *, head, base, synthetic):
+    from .policy import ACCEPTED_RELEASE
+    values = asdict(context) if isinstance(context, CheckContext) else context
+    if (values.get("repository") != REPOSITORY or values.get("accepted_release") != ACCEPTED_RELEASE
+            or values.get("event") != "pull_request" or values.get("head_sha") != head
+            or values.get("base_sha") != base or values.get("checked_sha") != synthetic
+            or type(values.get("run_id")) is not int or values["run_id"] <= 0
+            or type(values.get("run_attempt")) is not int or values["run_attempt"] <= 0
+            or type(values.get("pr_number")) is not int or values["pr_number"] <= 0):
+        raise HardeningError("E_CONTEXT", "Evidence is not for the current genuine PR head/base/synthetic")
+
+
+def main(argv=None):
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument("--repo", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--event-file", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--report", required=True)
+    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
+    try:
+        repo = GitRepo(args.repo)
+        candidate = repo.run("rev-parse", "HEAD").strip().decode("ascii")
+        context = capture_context(repo, candidate, args.event_file)
+        if context.event not in {"pull_request", "push"}:
+            raise HardeningError("E_CONTEXT", "Required check contexts accept only genuine PR merges or main pushes")
+        write_report(args.report, {"format": "Permansson.Hardening.CIContext.v1", **asdict(context)})
+        return 0
+    except HardeningError as exc:
+        write_report(args.report, {"format": "Permansson.Hardening.CIContext.v1", "status": "FAIL", "error_code": exc.code, "message": str(exc)})
+        return exc.exit_code

+"""Derive the frozen inventory from accepted canonical Git objects."""
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+import hashlib
+import json
+import re
+
+from .policy import (
+    MANIFEST_LIMIT, PRODUCTION_POLICY, PROTECTED_BLOB_LIMIT,
+    PROTECTED_TOTAL_LIMIT, _InventoryPolicy,
+)
+from .reports import HardeningError
+
+_OID = re.compile(r"[0-9a-f]{40}\Z")
+_SHA256 = re.compile(r"[0-9a-f]{64}\Z")
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class ProtectedEntry:
+    path: bytes
+    group: str
+    mode: str
+    oid: str
+    sha256: str
+    size: int
+
+
+def _invalid(message):
+    raise HardeningError("E_POLICY_INVENTORY", message)
+
+
+def _pairs(pairs):
+    obj = {}
+    for key, value in pairs:
+        if key in obj:
+            _invalid("duplicate JSON key: " + repr(key))
+        obj[key] = value
+    return obj
+
+
+def parse_manifest(payload: bytes, policy: _InventoryPolicy):
+    """Strict parser exposed for direct malformed-policy tests."""
+    if len(payload) > MANIFEST_LIMIT:
+        raise HardeningError("E_LIMIT", "reference manifest exceeds budget")
+    try:
+        data = json.loads(payload.decode("utf-8"), object_pairs_hook=_pairs,
+                          parse_constant=lambda value: (_ for _ in ()).throw(ValueError(value)))
+    except (UnicodeError, ValueError) as exc:
+        _invalid("invalid reference JSON: " + str(exc))
+    if not isinstance(data, dict):
+        _invalid("reference manifest must be an object")
+    expected = {
+        "schema_version": 1, "version": "0.2.0", "mode": "final",
+        "baseline_sha": policy.historical_baseline,
+        "selected_source_sha": policy.research_source,
+        "accepted_source_sha": policy.research_source,
+    }
+    for key, value in expected.items():
+        if type(data.get(key)) is not type(value) or data.get(key) != value:
+            _invalid("reference identity/schema mismatch: " + key)
+    rows = data.get("protected_files")
+    if not isinstance(rows, list) or len(rows) != policy.historical_count:
+        _invalid("historical inventory count mismatch")
+    seen = set()
+    for row in rows:
+        if not isinstance(row, dict):
+            _invalid("historical row must be an object")
+        path = row.get("path")
+        if not isinstance(path, str):
+            _invalid("historical path must be text")
+        try:
+            raw = path.encode("ascii")
+        except UnicodeError:
+            _invalid("historical policy paths must be ASCII")
+        if (not raw or raw.startswith(b"/") or b"\\" in raw or b"\x00" in raw
+                or any(part in (b"", b".", b"..") for part in raw.split(b"/"))
+                or b":" in raw or raw in seen):
+            _invalid("invalid or duplicate historical path: " + repr(path))
+        seen.add(raw)
+        if row.get("mode") not in ("100644", "100755"):
+            _invalid("historical entry is not a regular-file mode")
+        if not isinstance(row.get("git_blob_sha1"), str) or not _OID.fullmatch(row["git_blob_sha1"]):
+            _invalid("malformed historical blob identity")
+        if not isinstance(row.get("sha256"), str) or not _SHA256.fullmatch(row["sha256"]):
+            _invalid("malformed historical SHA-256")
+    return data
+
+
+def _under(path: bytes, root: bytes):
+    return path == root or path.startswith(root + b"/")
+
+

+    """Private tiny-policy seam for real Git fixtures; never selected by CLI."""
+    try:
+        authority = repo.commit(policy.accepted_release)
+    except HardeningError as exc:
+        raise HardeningError("E_REFERENCE_MISSING", "accepted authority commit is absent") from exc
+    if authority.tree != policy.accepted_tree:
+        raise HardeningError("E_REFERENCE_ID", "accepted authority tree differs from fixed pin")
+    tree = repo.tree(policy.accepted_release)
+    manifest_entry = tree.get(policy.manifest_path)
+    if manifest_entry is None:
+        raise HardeningError("E_REFERENCE_MISSING", "accepted manifest is absent")
+    if manifest_entry.object_type != "blob" or manifest_entry.mode != "100644":
+        _invalid("accepted manifest has invalid type/mode")
+    payload = repo.blob(manifest_entry.oid, limit=MANIFEST_LIMIT)
+    if hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest() != policy.manifest_sha256:
+        _invalid("accepted manifest digest differs from fixed pin")
+    data = parse_manifest(payload, policy)
+    entries = []
+    used = set()
+    total = 0
+    for row in data["protected_files"]:
+        path = row["path"].encode("ascii")
+        actual = tree.get(path)
+        if (actual is None or actual.object_type != "blob" or actual.mode != row["mode"]
+                or actual.oid != row["git_blob_sha1"]):
+            _invalid("historical Git metadata differs: " + repr(row["path"]))
+        blob = repo.blob(actual.oid, limit=PROTECTED_BLOB_LIMIT)
+        digest = hashlib.sha256(blob).hexdigest()
+        if digest != row["sha256"]:
+            _invalid("historical blob digest differs: " + repr(row["path"]))
+        entries.append(ProtectedEntry(path, "historical", actual.mode, actual.oid, digest, len(blob)))

+        total += len(blob)

+    for path in sorted(release_paths):
+        actual = tree.get(path)
+        if actual is None or actual.object_type != "blob" or actual.mode not in ("100644", "100755"):
+            _invalid("release inventory member has invalid type/mode: " + repr(path))
+        blob = repo.blob(actual.oid, limit=PROTECTED_BLOB_LIMIT)
+        entries.append(ProtectedEntry(path, "release_v020", actual.mode, actual.oid,
+                                      hashlib.sha256(blob).hexdigest(), len(blob)))
+        total += len(blob)
+        if total > PROTECTED_TOTAL_LIMIT:
+            raise HardeningError("E_LIMIT", "combined protected bytes exceed budget")
+    if len(entries) != policy.historical_count + policy.release_count:
+        _invalid("union inventory count mismatch")
+    return tuple(sorted(entries, key=lambda entry: entry.path))
+
+
+def load_reference_inventory(repo) -> tuple[ProtectedEntry, ...]:
+    return _load_reference_inventory(repo, PRODUCTION_POLICY)
+
+
+def inventory_digest(entries):
+    payload = [{"path": e.path.decode("ascii"), "group": e.group, "mode": e.mode,
+                "oid": e.oid, "sha256": e.sha256, "size": e.size} for e in entries]
+    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=True, sort_keys=True,
+                                    separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()

+"""Compare canonical candidate objects with the immutable accepted inventory."""
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+import hashlib
+
+from .inventory import inventory_digest, load_reference_inventory
+from .policy import (
+    ACCEPTED_RELEASE, ACCEPTED_RELEASE_TREE, CLOSED_ROOTS, DIFFERENCE_LIMIT,
+    PROTECTED_BLOB_LIMIT, PROTECTED_TOTAL_LIMIT, SENSITIVE_ROOTS,
+)
+from .reports import HardeningError
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class PreservationDifference:
+    code: str
+    path: bytes
+    message: str
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class PreservationResult:
+    differences: tuple[PreservationDifference, ...]
+    protected_count: int
+    protected_bytes: int
+
+    @property
+    def status(self):
+        return "FAIL" if self.differences else "PASS"
+
+    @property
+    def error_code(self):
+        return self.differences[0].code if self.differences else None
+
+    def require_pass(self):
+        if self.differences:
+            first = self.differences[0]
+            failure = HardeningError(first.code, first.message + ": " + repr(first.path))
+            failure.details = {
+                "scope": "canonical_commit_objects",
+                "protected_count": self.protected_count,
+                "differences": [{"code": diff.code,
+                                 "path": diff.path.decode("utf-8", "backslashreplace"),
+                                 "message": diff.message} for diff in self.differences],
+            }
+            raise failure
+
+
+def _under(path, root):
+    return path == root or path.startswith(root + b"/")
+
+
+def compare_preserved(reference, reference_tree, candidate_tree, read_blob,
+                      closed_roots=CLOSED_ROOTS):
+    """Pure comparison. Never dereference repository filesystem paths.
+
+    Primary precedence: ancestor/type, missing, mode, content, closed addition.
+    All differences use deterministic (precedence,path) ordering and are bounded.
+    """
+    differences = []
+    precedence = {"E_PROTECTED_TYPE": 0, "E_PROTECTED_MISSING": 1,
+                  "E_PROTECTED_MODE": 2, "E_PROTECTED_CONTENT": 3,
+                  "E_CLOSED_ADDITION": 4}
+
+    def add(code, path, message):
+        if len(differences) >= DIFFERENCE_LIMIT:
+            raise HardeningError("E_LIMIT", "preservation difference budget exceeded")
+        differences.append(PreservationDifference(code, path, message))
+
+    replacement_paths = set()
+    targets = set(closed_roots)
+    reference_directories = {path for path, entry in reference_tree.items()
+                             if entry.object_type == "tree"}
+    for path in reference_tree:
+        parts = path.split(b"/")
+        reference_directories.update(b"/".join(parts[:i]) for i in range(1, len(parts)))
+    for entry in reference:
+        parts = entry.path.split(b"/")
+        targets.update(b"/".join(parts[:i]) for i in range(1, len(parts)))
+    for ancestor in sorted(targets):
+        actual = candidate_tree.get(ancestor)
+        # Callers may provide leaves alone (private fixtures) or full topology.
+        if (actual is not None and actual.object_type != "tree"
+                and ancestor in reference_directories):
+            replacement_paths.add(ancestor)
+            add("E_PROTECTED_TYPE", ancestor, "protected directory replaced by a leaf")
+
+    total = 0
+    for entry in reference:
+        if any(entry.path.startswith(path + b"/") for path in replacement_paths):
+            continue
+        actual = candidate_tree.get(entry.path)
+        if actual is None:
+            # A file replaced by a directory is a topology/type change.
+            if any(path.startswith(entry.path + b"/") for path in candidate_tree):
+                add("E_PROTECTED_TYPE", entry.path, "protected file replaced by a directory")
+            else:
+                add("E_PROTECTED_MISSING", entry.path, "protected path is absent")
+            continue
+        if actual.object_type != "blob" or actual.mode not in ("100644", "100755"):
+            add("E_PROTECTED_TYPE", entry.path, "protected regular file changed type")
+            continue
+        if actual.mode != entry.mode:
+            add("E_PROTECTED_MODE", entry.path, "protected regular file changed mode")
+        blob = read_blob(actual.oid, limit=PROTECTED_BLOB_LIMIT)
+        total += len(blob)
+        if total > PROTECTED_TOTAL_LIMIT:
+            raise HardeningError("E_LIMIT", "candidate protected bytes exceed budget")
+        if (actual.oid != entry.oid or len(blob) != entry.size
+                or hashlib.sha256(blob).hexdigest() != entry.sha256):
+            add("E_PROTECTED_CONTENT", entry.path, "protected canonical bytes changed")
+    pinned = {entry.path for entry in reference}
+    for path in sorted(set(reference_tree) - set(candidate_tree) - pinned):
+        if any(_under(path, root) for root in closed_roots):
+            if not any(path.startswith(ancestor + b"/") for ancestor in replacement_paths):
+                add("E_PROTECTED_MISSING", path, "closed-root reference member is absent")
+    for path in sorted(set(candidate_tree) - set(reference_tree)):
+        if path in replacement_paths:
+            continue
+        if any(_under(path, root) for root in closed_roots):
+            add("E_CLOSED_ADDITION", path, "new tracked path inside a closed root")
+    differences.sort(key=lambda diff: (precedence[diff.code], diff.path))
+    return PreservationResult(tuple(differences), len(reference), total)
+
+
+def sensitive_changes(reference_tree, candidate_tree):
+    return [path.decode("utf-8", "backslashreplace")
+            for path in sorted(set(reference_tree) | set(candidate_tree))
+            if any(_under(path, root) for root in SENSITIVE_ROOTS)
+            and reference_tree.get(path) != candidate_tree.get(path)]
+
+
+def verify_preservation(repo, candidate):
+    repo.validate_candidate(candidate, accepted_sha=ACCEPTED_RELEASE,
+                            accepted_tree=ACCEPTED_RELEASE_TREE)
+    reference = load_reference_inventory(repo)
+    trusted_tree = repo.tree_entries(ACCEPTED_RELEASE)
+    candidate_tree = repo.tree_entries(candidate)
+    result = compare_preserved(reference, trusted_tree, candidate_tree, repo.blob)
+    result.require_pass()
+    return {
+        "scope": "canonical_commit_objects",
+        "completed_stages": ["reference_inventory", "protected_comparison", "closed_root_membership"],
+        "protected_count": result.protected_count,
+        "protected_bytes": result.protected_bytes,
+        "inventory_sha256": inventory_digest(reference),
+        "trust_sensitive_changes": sensitive_changes(trusted_tree, candidate_tree),
+        "trust_boundary": "Candidate-owned checker and workflow require independent review.",
+    }
+
+
+def validate_maintenance_scope(repo, candidate):
+    """One-time acceptance check; deliberately absent from the permanent gate."""
+    baseline = repo.tree_entries(ACCEPTED_RELEASE)
+    target = repo.tree_entries(candidate)
+    paths = set(baseline) | set(target)
+    for path in sorted(paths):
+        if (path in (b"PermanssonLean.lean", b"PermanssonResearch.lean")
+                or _under(path, b"PermanssonLean") or _under(path, b"PermanssonResearch")):
+            if baseline.get(path) != target.get(path):
+                raise HardeningError("E_MAINTENANCE_SCOPE", "Lean source changed: " + repr(path))
+
+
+def main(argv=None):
+    from .reports import run_cli
+    return run_cli("frozen-source-preservation", argv, verify_preservation)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

+"""Bounded, atomic machine reports and explicit verification failures."""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import dataclasses
+import json
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+import platform
+import tempfile
+
+
+class HardeningError(Exception):
+    def __init__(self, code: str, message: str, exit_code: int = 1):
+        super().__init__(message)
+        self.code, self.message, self.exit_code = code, message, exit_code
+
+
+def strict_json(data: bytes | str, code: str = "E_MANIFEST_FORMAT"):
+    def pairs(items):
+        result = {}
+        for key, value in items:
+            if key in result:
+                raise HardeningError(code, f"Duplicate JSON key: {key!r}")
+            result[key] = value
+        return result
+    try:
+        return json.loads(data, object_pairs_hook=pairs,
+                          parse_constant=lambda value: (_ for _ in ()).throw(ValueError(value)))
+    except (ValueError, UnicodeError, TypeError) as exc:
+        raise HardeningError(code, f"Invalid JSON: {str(exc)[:300]}") from exc
+
+
+def write_report(path, payload):
+    target = Path(path).resolve()
+    for ancestor in target.parents:
+        if (ancestor / ".git").exists():
+            relative = target.relative_to(ancestor)
+            # Reports are scratch outputs. Keep them outside source directories;
+            # resolving first also catches a scratch-directory symlink into source.
+            if relative.parts[0] not in {".hardening-reports", "artifacts"}:
+                raise HardeningError("E_REPORT", "Use external scratch or a repository scratch-output directory", 2)
+            break
+    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    encoded = (json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True, indent=2, ensure_ascii=True, allow_nan=False) + "\n").encode()
+    if len(encoded) > 8 * 1024 * 1024:
+        raise HardeningError("E_LIMIT", "Report exceeds 8 MiB")
+    fd, temporary = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=".report-", dir=target.parent)
+    try:
+        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as stream:
+            stream.write(encoded)
+            stream.flush()
+            os.fsync(stream.fileno())
+        os.replace(temporary, target)
+    finally:
+        if os.path.exists(temporary):
+            os.unlink(temporary)
+
+
+def check_report(check, context=None, status="PASS", error=None, **details):
+    ctx = dataclasses.asdict(context) if dataclasses.is_dataclass(context) else (context or {})
+    return {"format": "Permansson.Hardening.Check.v1", "schema_version": 1,
+            "check": check, "status": status,
+            "error_code": getattr(error, "code", None),
+            "message": str(error)[:4000] if error else None,
+            "context": ctx, "runtime": {"python": platform.python_version(), "platform": platform.system()},
+            **details}
+
+
+def run_cli(check, argv, verify_callback):
+    from .git_objects import GitRepo
+    from .ci_context import capture_context
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=check)
+    parser.add_argument("--repo", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--candidate", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--report", required=True)
+    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
+    context = None
+    try:
+        repo = GitRepo(args.repo)
+        context = capture_context(repo, args.candidate)
+        result = verify_callback(repo, args.candidate)
+        if dataclasses.is_dataclass(result):
+            result = dataclasses.asdict(result)
+        payload = check_report(check, context, completed_stages=["context", "verification"], details=result)
+        code = 0
+    except HardeningError as exc:
+        payload = check_report(check, context, "BLOCKED" if exc.exit_code == 3 else "FAIL", exc,
+                               details=getattr(exc, "details", {}))
+        code = exc.exit_code
+    except Exception as exc:
+        payload = check_report(check, context, "FAIL", HardeningError("E_UNEXPECTED", str(exc)))
+        code = 1
+    write_report(args.report, payload)
+    print(f"{check}: {payload['status']}" + (f" {payload['error_code']}" if payload['error_code'] else ""))
+    return code

+"""Execute a fixed suite with fail-closed case mapping and result accounting."""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import io
+import json
+import platform
+from pathlib import Path
+import sys
+import unittest
+
+from .reports import HardeningError, strict_json, write_report
+
+SUITES = {
+    "reference": "verification.integrity.tests.test_reference",
+    "preservation": "verification.integrity.tests.test_preservation",
+    "tex": "verification.integrity.tests.test_tex",
+    "context": "verification.integrity.tests.test_context",
+    "workflow": "verification.integrity.tests.test_workflow",
+    "archive": "verification.archive.tests.test_archive",
+}
+
+REQUIREMENTS = {}
+for prefix, count, suite in (("REF", 15, "reference"), ("PRES", 23, "preservation"),
+                             ("TEX", 20, "tex"), ("ARCH", 27, "archive")):
+    for number in range(1, count + 1):
+        REQUIREMENTS[f"{prefix}-{number:02}"] = (suite, "integration" if prefix == "ARCH" and number in {14, 23} else "unit")
+for number in range(1, 12):
+    level = "unit" if number in {3, 6, 7, 9} else "review" if number == 10 else "live_pr"
+    suite = "context" if number in {3, 9} else "workflow" if number in {6, 7} else None
+    REQUIREMENTS[f"CI-{number:02}"] = (suite, level)
+for number in range(1, 13):
+    REQUIREMENTS[f"OPS-{number:02}"] = (None, "authorized_rollout")
+
+
+def flatten(suite):
+    for item in suite:
+        if isinstance(item, unittest.TestSuite):
+            yield from flatten(item)
+        else:
+            yield item
+
+
+def validate_mapping(registry, suite, discovered):
+    return _validate_mapping(registry, suite, discovered, REQUIREMENTS)
+
+
+def _validate_mapping(registry, suite, discovered, contract):
+    rows = registry.get("cases", [])
+    if {row.get("id") for row in rows} != set(contract):
+        raise HardeningError("E_REPORT", "Registry differs from the complete required case inventory")
+    for row in rows:
+        if (row.get("suite"), row.get("level")) != contract[row["id"]]:
+            raise HardeningError("E_REPORT", "A requirement's suite or evidence level changed")
+    if not discovered:
+        raise HardeningError("E_REPORT", "Zero tests discovered")
+    if any("_FailedTest" in name for name in discovered):
+        raise HardeningError("E_REPORT", "Test loading failed")
+    requirements = [item for item in rows if item.get("suite") == suite and item["level"] == "unit"]
+    if not requirements:
+        raise HardeningError("E_REPORT", "Required executable-case mappings are absent")
+    ids = [item["id"] for item in registry["cases"]]
+    if len(ids) != len(set(ids)):
+        raise HardeningError("E_REPORT", "Duplicate requirement IDs")
+    methods = {}
+    for case in requirements:
+        names = case.get("methods", [])
+        if not names or len(names) != len(set(names)):
+            raise HardeningError("E_REPORT", f"Missing or duplicate mapping for {case['id']}")
+        if len(names) > 1 and not case.get("mapping_explanation"):
+            raise HardeningError("E_REPORT", "Multiple mappings require an explanation")
+        for name in names:
+            if name not in discovered:
+                raise HardeningError("E_REPORT", f"Mapped method was not discovered: {name}")
+            methods.setdefault(name, []).append(case["id"])
+    for name, cases in methods.items():
+        if len(cases) > 1:
+            relevant = [case for case in requirements if case["id"] in cases]
+            if not all(case.get("mapping_explanation") for case in relevant):
+                raise HardeningError("E_REPORT", "Shared case mapping needs an explanation")
+    if set(discovered) - methods.keys():
+        # Additional positive controls are permitted, but must be explicitly declared.
+        controls = set(registry.get("controls", {}).get(suite, []))
+        if set(discovered) - methods.keys() - controls:
+            raise HardeningError("E_REPORT", "Discovered methods lack requirement/control mapping")
+    return methods
+
+
+class RecordedResult(unittest.TextTestResult):
+    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
+        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
+        self.records = []
+        self.subtest_count = 0
+
+    def addSuccess(self, test):
+        super().addSuccess(test)
+        self.records.append({"method": test.id(), "status": "PASS"})
+
+    def addFailure(self, test, err):
+        super().addFailure(test, err)
+        self.records.append({"method": test.id(), "status": "FAIL"})
+
+    def addError(self, test, err):
+        super().addError(test, err)
+        self.records.append({"method": test.id(), "status": "ERROR"})
+
+    def addSkip(self, test, reason):
+        super().addSkip(test, reason)
+        self.records.append({"method": test.id(), "status": "SKIP", "reason": reason})
+
+    def addSubTest(self, test, subtest, err):
+        super().addSubTest(test, subtest, err)
+        self.subtest_count += 1
+        self.records.append({"method": test.id(), "subtest": str(subtest), "status": "PASS" if err is None else "FAIL"})
+
+    def addExpectedFailure(self, test, err):
+        super().addExpectedFailure(test, err)
+        self.records.append({"method": test.id(), "status": "EXPECTED_FAILURE"})
+
+
+def validate_result(result, discovered, mapping):
+    if (not result.wasSuccessful() or result.skipped or result.expectedFailures
+            or result.testsRun != len(discovered) or not result.testsRun):
+        raise HardeningError("E_REPORT", "Suite failed, skipped, or did not execute every discovered method")
+    executed = {row["method"] for row in result.records if "subtest" not in row and row["status"] == "PASS"}
+    if set(discovered) != executed:
+        raise HardeningError("E_REPORT", "Successful result records do not cover discovered methods")
+    return sorted({case for name in executed for case in mapping.get(name, [])})
+
+
+def main(argv=None):
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument("--suite", required=True, choices=tuple(SUITES))
+    parser.add_argument("--report", required=True)
+    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
+    result = None
+    mapping = {}
+    payload = {"format": "Permansson.Hardening.Tests.v1", "schema_version": 1, "suite": args.suite}
+    try:
+        from .git_objects import GitRepo
+        from .ci_context import capture_context
+        from dataclasses import asdict
+        repo = GitRepo(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2])
+        candidate = repo.run("rev-parse", "HEAD").strip().decode("ascii")
+        payload["context"] = asdict(capture_context(repo, candidate))
+        payload["runtime"] = {"python": platform.python_version(), "git": repo.run("--version").strip().decode()}
+        try:
+            repo.run("diff", "--quiet", "HEAD", "--")
+            tracked_clean = True
+        except HardeningError:
+            tracked_clean = False
+        payload["execution_tracked_clean"] = tracked_clean
+        if not tracked_clean and payload["context"]["event"] != "local":
+            raise HardeningError("E_CONTEXT", "Tests cannot execute dirty tracked sources in CI")
+        registry = strict_json(Path(__file__).with_name("test_coverage.json").read_bytes(), "E_REPORT")
+        loader = unittest.TestLoader()
+        suite = loader.loadTestsFromName(SUITES[args.suite])
+        discovered = [case.id() for case in flatten(suite)]
+        if loader.errors:
+            raise HardeningError("E_REPORT", "Test loader errors: " + str(loader.errors)[:2000])
+        mapping = validate_mapping(registry, args.suite, discovered)
+        result = unittest.TextTestRunner(verbosity=2, resultclass=RecordedResult).run(suite)
+        covered = validate_result(result, discovered, mapping)
+        payload.update(status="PASS", error_code=None, covered_requirements=covered)
+        code = 0
+    except (HardeningError, OSError, KeyError, TypeError) as exc:
+        payload.update(status="FAIL", error_code=getattr(exc, "code", "E_REPORT"), message=str(exc)[:4000])
+        code = getattr(exc, "exit_code", 1)
+    if result:
+        for row in result.records:
+            row["requirements"] = mapping.get(row["method"], [])
+        payload.update(methods_run=result.testsRun, subtests_run=result.subtest_count,

+"""Private real-Git fixtures; no fixture authority is exposed by production CLI."""
+
+from dataclasses import replace
+import hashlib
+import json
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+import shutil
+import subprocess
+import tempfile
+
+from verification.integrity.git_objects import GitRepo
+from verification.integrity.inventory import _load_reference_inventory
+from verification.integrity.policy import _InventoryPolicy, CLOSED_ROOTS
+from verification.integrity.preservation import compare_preserved
+
+
+def json_bytes(data):
+    return (json.dumps(data, sort_keys=True, indent=2) + "\n").encode()
+
+
+class GitFixture:
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.temporary = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="permansson-integrity-fixture-")
+        self.root = Path(self.temporary.name)
+        env = {key: value for key, value in os.environ.items() if not key.startswith("GIT_")}
+        subprocess.run([shutil.which("git"), "init", "-q", str(self.root)],
+                       check=True, capture_output=True, env=env)
+        self.repo = GitRepo(self.root)
+        # Raw Git paths can be legal in objects while impossible to materialize
+        # on Windows. These fixtures never check out the adversarial names.
+        self.repo.run("config", "core.protectNTFS", "false")
+        self.repo.env["GIT_INDEX_FILE"] = str(self.root / ".git" / "fixture-index")
+        self.counter = 0
+        self.files = {
+            b"PermanssonLean/Regime/Constitution.lean": b"theorem original : True := True.intro\n",
+            b"PermanssonResearch/ReverseSolver/C10ReceiptSemantics.lean": b"-- D0 original\n",
+            b"paper/original.md": b"Accepted paper\n",
+            b"PermanssonLean.lean": b"import PermanssonLean.Regime.Constitution\n",
+        }
+        rows = [{"path": path.decode(), "mode": "100644", "git_blob_sha1": self.blob(data),
+                 "sha256": hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()} for path, data in sorted(self.files.items())]
+        self.manifest = {
+            "schema_version": 1, "version": "0.2.0", "mode": "final",
+            "baseline_sha": "1" * 40, "selected_source_sha": "2" * 40,
+            "accepted_source_sha": "2" * 40, "protected_files": rows,
+        }
+        manifest = json_bytes(self.manifest)
+        self.files.update({
+            b"release/v0.2.0/manifest.json": manifest,
+            b"release/v0.2.0/manuscript.json": b'{"F1.MA2":"OPEN"}\n',
+            b"release/v0.2.0/output.tex": b"Original equation\n",
+            b"release/Permansson_v0.2.0_research-kit.zip": b"fixture ZIP\n",
+            b"release/Permansson_v0.2.0_research-kit.zip.sha256": b"original checksum\n",
+        })
+        self.accepted = self.commit({path: ("100644", data) for path, data in self.files.items()}, parent=None)
+        self.repo.run("update-ref", "refs/heads/main", self.accepted)
+        self.repo.run("symbolic-ref", "HEAD", "refs/heads/main")
+        self.policy = _InventoryPolicy(
+            self.accepted, self.repo.commit(self.accepted).tree, "1" * 40, "2" * 40,
+            hashlib.sha256(manifest).hexdigest(), historical_count=4, release_count=5,
+        )
+
+    def close(self):
+        self.repo._config.cleanup()
+        self.temporary.cleanup()
+
+    def blob(self, data):
+        return self.repo.run("hash-object", "-w", "--stdin", input=data).strip().decode()
+
+    def commit(self, changes, parent="accepted"):
+        if parent == "accepted":
+            parent = self.accepted
+        self.repo.run("read-tree", parent if parent else "--empty")
+        existing = self.repo.tree(parent) if parent else {}
+        records = []
+        zero = "0" * 40
+        for path, replacement in changes.items():
+            # Root replacement has to remove all old descendants from the index.
+            for child in sorted(existing):
+                if child.startswith(path + b"/"):
+                    records.append(b"0 " + zero.encode() + b"\t" + child + b"\0")
+            if replacement is None:
+                records.append(b"0 " + zero.encode() + b"\t" + path + b"\0")
+            else:
+                mode, content = replacement
+                oid = content if isinstance(content, str) else self.blob(content)
+                records.append(mode.encode() + b" " + oid.encode() + b"\t" + path + b"\0")
+        if records:
+            self.repo.run("update-index", "-z", "--index-info", input=b"".join(records))
+        tree = self.repo.run("write-tree").strip().decode()
+        self.counter += 1
+        args = ["-c", "user.name=Integrity Fixture", "-c", "user.email=fixture@example.invalid",
+                "commit-tree", tree, "-m", "fixture " + str(self.counter)]
+        if parent:
+            args.extend(["-p", parent])
+        return self.repo.run(*args).strip().decode()
+
+    def compare(self, candidate):
+        reference = _load_reference_inventory(self.repo, self.policy)
+        return compare_preserved(reference, self.repo.tree(self.accepted),
+                                 self.repo.tree(candidate), self.repo.blob,
+                                 closed_roots=self.policy.closed_roots)
+
+    def malformed_authority(self, manifest=None, *, files=None, **policy_changes):
+        """Create an explicit private authority to reach post-hash parser checks."""
+        payload = manifest if isinstance(manifest, bytes) else json_bytes(manifest or self.manifest)
+        changes = {self.policy.manifest_path: ("100644", payload)}
+        if files:
+            changes.update(files)
+        commit = self.commit(changes)
+        return replace(self.policy, accepted_release=commit,
+                       accepted_tree=self.repo.commit(commit).tree,
+                       manifest_sha256=hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest(), **policy_changes)

+class ContextTests(unittest.TestCase):
